# Preface {.unnumbered}

*A Python Companion to Intermediate Macroeconomics* is a set of computational notebooks. Each notebook takes one chapter of an
intermediate macroeconomics course and rebuilds its figures in Python, so that you can
**see the data** and **play with the models**.

## How to use this book

- **On this website** you can read every chapter, see all the figures, hover over the data
  points, and move the precomputed sliders under each model figure.
- **In Google Colab** you can run the code yourself. Click the *Open in Colab* badge at the
  top of a chapter, then choose *Runtime → Run all*. In Colab every model figure gets live
  sliders and buttons that recompute the model as you move them, and every "Your turn"
  exercise can be tried in an empty code cell.
- No installation is needed: Colab already has `numpy`, `pandas`, `plotly` and `ipywidgets`.
  The data are read directly from this book's GitHub repository.

## About the figures

Each chapter replicates the key elements of the figures of the corresponding textbook
chapter. Data figures are rebuilt with the latest available data, so the numbers may
differ slightly from the printed figures. A crosswalk table at the top of every chapter
links each notebook figure to the textbook figure it replicates.
